summary: 1934 Aermotor steel tower in Payette National Forest, NRHP-listed in 1994, still staffed in recent summers.

facts.design: Aermotor 721 steel tower, 7x7 ft steel cab, 85 ft tall

access.note: Active Forest Service lookout, drive-up access per idahofirelookouts.com; not a public rental

evidence.supports: Built 1934, last active tower on Payette NF, staffed every summer
evidence.quote: The last active fire tower on the Fayette National Forest, Carey Dome Lookout was placed into service in 1934.

evidence.supports: Aermotor tower, 85 ft, 7x7 cab, log cabin 1943, weather station, NRHP listing, location 9 miles north of Burgdorf Guard Station
evidence.quote: The tower is an Aermotor Company steel tower assembled in 1934, which has a 7 by 7 feet (2.1 m x 2.1 m) steel cab at the top. It is 85 feet (26 m) tall from ground level to top of the cab. ... located in Payette National Forest, 9 miles north of United States Forest Service Burgdorf Guard Station, near Burgdorf in Idaho County, Idaho. ... Added to NRHP March 25, 1994. ... The log cabin was built in 1943. ... The weather station was installed in the 1950s or before.

evidence.supports: Known staff list and drive-up/staffed status
evidence.quote:
Drive Up Staffed
Elevation: 7681' Payette National Forest

evidence.supports: 72-ft steel Aermotor tower, staffed every summer, NHLR listing
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, this 72' steel Aermotor tower and accompanying ground log cabin living quarters are staffed every summer.

corrections.why: idahofirelookouts.com gives 7681 ft vs NHLR's 7,667 ft; minor discrepancy, not corrected in story

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says 72 ft tower; Wikipedia (citing the NRHP nomination) says 85 ft ground-to-cab. Used the NRHP/Wikipedia figure as more authoritative; noted discrepancy exists.

notes_for_editor: Height and elevation figures differ slightly between NHLR/idahofirelookouts (7,667-7,681 ft; 72 ft tower) and Wikipedia/NRHP nomination (85 ft ground-to-cab). Did not independently pull the NRHP PDF itself (John F. Elliott, 1992) for primary confirmation; Wikipedia's summary of it was used instead.
